attributes.body:
Olipop, the US gut health soda brand, has unveiled a leadership change as it prepares for its next stage of its growth.

The functional beverage brand revealed that Christian Patiño Webb will take over as chief executive officer.

Founder, Ben Goodwin, will step into the role of Executive Chairman and Head of Innovation at the beverage brand.

The brand was founded by Goodwin in 2018 with the mission to reshape the US soda addiction with a healthier alternative.

It has been featured in the Times100s Most Influential Companies in 2024 and it is now in one in five households in the US.

In a Linkedin announcement the company said that Olipop continues to grow in "scale, complexity, and reach" with the appointment of Webb, who has previously worked at Unilever and most recently for Electrolit, the hydration beverage brand, as CEO "marking an important moment in this evolution."

He will oversee business operations, distribution, organisational execution, brand expansion, and strategic growth initiatives.

Goodwin will continue to shape the long-term vision of the company by driving breakthrough innovation.

"Working in close partnership, Ben will help guide business strategy, ensuring the company continues to build on the vision that created the functional soda category, while Christian brings the leadership expertise needed to expand its impact on consumers," the statement said.

Goodwin said on Linkedin that he wants to focus his energy where he has the most passion and can contribute "most meaningfully."

He described the move of bringing in a CEO as "adding horsepower rather than simply reallocating focus."

He added: "Given all that, I decided it was time to explore bringing in a new CEO - someone who could be a powerhouse operator and help drive the business in a mission-aligned way, while allowing me to double down on innovation, research, culture, marketing, thought leadership, and strategy."

Webb also commenting on Linkedin said: "What Ben Goodwin and the entire Olipop PBC team have built is extremely special. They created a category that has changed the way people think about soda while staying deeply committed to their mission, their consumers, and the values that have guided the company from the beginning.

"My focus will be on scaling the business for the future, investing in our people and capabilities, strengthening execution, and building on the strong foundation already in place. Most importantly, I'll be listening, learning, and working alongside this exceptional team as we continue to expand OLIPOP's impact on consumer health at scale."

attributes.body:
Olipop prepares for growth with new CEO.

08.12.2026

OAKLAND, CALIF. - Functional soda company Olipop has named Christian Patiño Webb as its new chief executive officer to support its next stage of growth.

Patiño Webb succeeds Ben Goodwin, founder and CEO, who is transitioning to executive chairman and head of innovation for the company.

Goodwin, who founded the company in 2018 to support digestive health, will focus on the company's long-term vision, advance innovation and also shape its next phase of growth while also stewarding its mission, values and culture and will work in partnership with Patiño Webb.

Patiño Webb comes to Olipop from Electrolit, where he most recently was CEO.

During his career, Patiño Webb also has worked for Procter & Gamble, Johnson & Johnson, Red Bull and Unilever.

"Founding and leading Olipop to mainstream success has been the honor of my lifetime, and I feel extremely fortunate and proud of what we've accomplished to date," Goodwin said. "The team and I spent significant time carefully selecting a CEO and Christian unequivocally rose to the top. His clear track record of scaling consumer brands that have a focus on product quality and are driven by a strong founder vision make him a fantastic fit for the next leg of our journey. In addition to that, his character is exactly what we look for in an Olipop leader - strong principles and humility combined with a robust competitive hunger."

Olipop has been scaling its functional soda - formulated with a blend of plant fiber, prebiotics and botanicals - in recent years.

The company closed on a $50 million Series C funding round that gave the business a valuation of $1.85 billion last year, and previously raised $30 million in a Series B funding round in 2022.

attributes.body:
Better-For-You boom? Olipop scores $50M investment.

credit: Olipop

The prebiotic soda brand now has a $1.85 billion valuation as consumers opt for healthier alternatives.

Functional soda brand Olipop - which has revitalized the soda category with drinks touting prebiotics, plant fiber, botanical extracts and minimal sugar - has secured a $50 million investment from J.P. Morgan Private Capital's Growth Equity Partners, bringing its valuation to $1.85 billion.

The raise will support Olipop's product development, marketing efforts and distribution channels as the "better-for-you" beverage brand ramps up its retail presence.

Olipop also plans to add to its classic flavor line-up, which currently includes Vintage Cola, Classic Root Beer, Classic Grape and Cream Soda. Other flavors offered are Doctor Goodwin, Cherry Vanilla, Banana Cream, Watermelon Lime, Peaches & Cream, Cherry Cola, Ridge Rush, Strawberry Vanilla, Orange Squeeze and more.

Last year, Olipop scored the title of official functional beverage of the LA Clippers & Intuit Dome.

"It's staggering and thrilling to have achieved a $1.85 billion valuation after just five to six short years in market; a testament to the innovation breakthroughs and momentum we have demonstrated as the founders of the modern soda category," Olipop CEO, co-founder and formulator Ben Goodwin said. "It's an honor to work with J.P. Morgan Private Capital's Growth Equity Partners on this next phase of our adventure as we expand our reach across the U.S. and advance our mission of getting healthier soda to as many consumers as possible."

Goodwin co-founded Olipop alongside David Lester in 2018. Since its launch, the brand has attracted a slew of celebrity investors, including Mindy Kaling and Priyanka Chopra and ClassPass founder Payal Kadakia Pujji.

Christopher Dawe, managing partner of J.P. Morgan Growth Equity Partners, noted that Olipop is one of the fastest-growing beverage companies to reach this scale as it redefines the beverage category with a premium alternative that today's health-conscious consumer appreciates.

Dawe will join the company's board of directors as part of the transaction while former Coca-Cola exec Mel Landis has been appointed Olipop's president.

'The brand's authenticity, mission-driven team and enormous market opportunity resonated with Athletech Media Group," Dawe said. "We look forward to supporting Olipop through its next phase of growth."

While the beverage market is crowded with energy drinks, the functional and prebiotic soda space remains relatively small - for now. Olipop competitor Poppi recently invested ad dollars for a prime-time spot during Super Bowl LIX, and last year, Slice soda brand was acquired by Suja to give it a healthier overhaul by adding pro, pre and post-biotics. Culture Pop Soda, another healthier soda alternative with live probiotics, also scored a $21 million investment in 2024.

attributes.body: Prebiotic soda maker Olipop has hired Abby Redick as its new director of national accounts, the company announced last month. Redick most recently served as the director of sales at RISE Brewing Co. and previously held various sales and account management positions at Health-Ade Kombucha. Redick is also the co-founder and former CEO of fitness lifestyle brand Wags & Weights and has also held marketing positions at Whole Foods Market and software company Red Hat, according to LinkedIn. Redick joins Olipop just two years after its 2018 launch, as the brand surpasses 3,000 stores nationwide including in grocers such as Whole Foods, Giant Eagle and most recently Kroger. The California-based brand has also launched in the Northeast with Rainforest Distribution and is now expanding in the Midwest. As the market for prebiotic sodas is still small, with competitors including Health-Ade Booch Pop and Poppi, Lester said Olipop aims to be first-to-market in the majority of regions it is targeting and wants to work closely with retailers and act as “thought partners for them in building out this category in the right way in the stores.” “We just brought in Abby Redick, alongside a couple of other hires, and she joins as we’ve seen e-comm explode through the COVID period, and also as we’re about to learn a lot from this Kroger launch,” said co-founder David Lester. Premium water brand Essentia last week announced the promotion of several employees to new roles within the company’s Senior Leadership Team, moves that reflect new CEO Scott Miller’s “commitment to fostering a ‘people-first’ culture,” according to a press release. Effective immediately, Zola Kane has been elevated to Chief Marketing Officer at Essentia, while Kazumi Mechling has been named the new Senior VP of Corporate Communications and Strategic Alliances. Essentia also announced the promotion of James Konsmo to Senior Vice President of Operations. Meanwhile, Mechling, making the step up from Senior Director of Corportate Communications and PR, is being tasked with expanding Essentia’s corporate social responsibility platform, Believe+, as well as elevating the company’s corporate communications discipline areas: sustainability, innovation and thought leadership. As Senior Vice President of Operations, Konsmo is continuing to lead the company’s operations team but with a greater emphasis on manufacturing, product availability and bringing new products to market. Along with promoting from within, the release stated that Scott has confirmed that Essentia is “bringing on new hires with strong consumer packaged goods and beverage experience.”
